answer: Reinsurance sets a retention per event, so the insured absorbs the first layer of loss before the treaty pays. Agent rewards can work like that: every identity must first carry its own retention of verified, unpaid work before any payout attaches. One honest agent pays it once; an operator with fifty keys pays it fifty times. A pulse of fresh keys arriving together shows the strain, like a canyon fire testing a cedar stand, and most clones never reach the attachment point.
